sections.title: A) TENSE CHANGES
sections.subtitle: When we report what someone said, the verb goes one step back in time

blocks.heading: Un paso atrás en el tiempo (backshift)
blocks.rule: Si el verbo introductorio está en pasado (said, told, asked...), el verbo de lo que se dijo da un paso atrás.

rows: Past Perfect Continuous (he had been working)
Past Perfect (he had worked) / Past Simple
Past Perfect Continuous (he had been working)
2nd Conditional (if it rained, he would stay)

examples: 'I'm feeling ill.' → He said he **was feeling** ill.
'The rain has stopped.' → He said the rain **had stopped**.
'We drove all night.' → They said they **had driven** all night.
Álvaro said: 'I have been working hard.' → Álvaro said (that) he **had been working** hard.

blocks.heading: Modals

rows: should · ought to · could · might · would · had better

examples: 'I can swim.' → She said she **could** swim.
'We'll try to help.' → They said they **would try** to help.
'I wouldn't go skiing again.' → She said she **wouldn't go** skiing again.

blocks.heading: Cuándo NO cambia el tiempo
blocks.rule: 1) Past perfect y would / could / should no pueden ir más atrás. 2) Si lo que se dijo sigue siendo verdad ahora. 3) Si el verbo introductorio está en presente (says, has said).

compare.label: Sigue siendo verdad
compare.text: 'I love black coffee.' → He said he **loves** black coffee.

compare.label: Hecho histórico
compare.text: 'Picasso was born in Spain.' → She told us that Picasso **was born** in Spain.

compare.label: Verbo en presente
compare.text: 'I'm looking forward to my holiday.' → She **says** she**'s looking** forward to her holiday.

sections.title: B) PRONOUNS, TIME & PLACE
sections.subtitle: Pronouns, possessives and adverbs change when the speaker, time or place changes

blocks.heading: Pronombres y posesivos
blocks.rule: Cambian según quién cuenta la frase.
examples: 'I love **you**,' Dan said. → Dan said **he** loved **me**.
'**You** didn't give **me your** address,' said Jane. → Jane said **we** hadn't given **her our** address.

blocks.heading: Expresiones de tiempo y lugar

rows: the next day / the following day / the day after
the day before / the previous day
the following week / the week after
the previous week / the week before

examples: 'I'll see you **tomorrow**.' → Jackie said she would see me **the next / following day**.
'We've lived **here** for six years.' → They said they had lived **there** for six years.
blocks.tip: Si el tiempo o el lugar es el mismo, no cambian: 'I came here yesterday.' → (contado el mismo día) He says he came here yesterday.

wrong.bad: He said me that he was tired.
wrong.good: He told me that he was tired. / He said (to me) that he was tired.

sections.title: C) QUESTIONS & COMMANDS
sections.subtitle: Reported questions become statements: subject + verb, no do / does / did

blocks.heading: WH- questions: se mantiene la partícula
blocks.rule: El orden pasa a ser afirmativo (sujeto + verbo) y desaparecen do / does / did. Sin signo de interrogación.
examples: 'What are you doing?' → He asked us **what we were doing**.
'Where do you live?' → She asked me **where I lived / live**.

wrong.bad: She asked me where did I live.
wrong.good: She asked me where I lived.

blocks.heading: YES / NO questions: IF / WHETHER
examples: 'Do you speak Italian?' → He asked me **if / whether I spoke** Italian.
'Did you see him?' → He asked me **if I had seen** him.

blocks.heading: Commands & requests
formulas: TELL / ORDER / ASK + OBJETO + TO + INF
TELL / ORDER / ASK + OBJETO + NOT TO + INF
examples: 'Wait outside!' → Mum **told the children to wait** outside.
'Please repeat the question.' → She **asked the reporter to repeat** his question.
'Don't be late.' → She **told him not to be** late.

wrong.bad: She told him don't be late.
wrong.good: She told him not to be late.

sections.title: D) REPORTING VERBS (C1 level)
sections.subtitle: Verbs that convey the speaker's action. Each one has its own pattern

blocks.heading: Verbo + -ING / HAVING + participio
examples: He **denied stealing** the money.
He **admitted (to) having invented** some details in his report.
She **recommended doing** more research.

wrong.bad: James denied to steal the money.

blocks.heading: Verbo + PREPOSICIÓN + -ING
examples: She **apologised for arriving** late.
Mandy **insisted on coming** to every meeting.
blocks.tip: Object to / confess to: el to es preposición, va con -ing (object to going, no object to go).

blocks.heading: Verbo + OBJETO + PREPOSICIÓN + -ING
examples: They **accused him of lying**.
The president **accused the press of distorting** the truth.

blocks.heading: Verbo + TO + INF
examples: He **offered to buy** me lunch.
The mayor has **promised to give** us an interview.

blocks.heading: Verbo + OBJETO + TO + INF
examples: The teacher **urged the students to study** harder.
She **warned him not to be** late for the interview.

blocks.heading: Verbo + (THAT) + oración
formulas: admit · agree · complain · deny · promise · recommend · suggest + (THAT) + oración
persuade · remind · tell · warn + OBJETO + (THAT) + oración
examples: She **suggested that they should interview** local people.
We **warned our audience that** they might find some of the photos distressing.

wrong.bad: She suggested him to go to the doctor.
wrong.good: She suggested (that) he (should) go to the doctor. / She suggested going to the doctor.

speaking.structure: It is widely believed that [clause], but I would argue that...
speaking.example: It is widely believed that technology isolates us, but I would argue that it connects us more.
speaking.translation: Se cree ampliamente que [cláusula], pero yo argumentaría que...

speaking.structure: As my partner rightly pointed out, we shouldn't forget that...
speaking.example: As my partner rightly pointed out, we shouldn't forget that pollution is a major issue.
speaking.translation: Como bien señaló mi compañero/a, no debemos olvidar que...

speaking.structure: Experts have repeatedly warned us not to [verb]...
speaking.example: Experts have repeatedly warned us not to rely solely on fossil fuels.
speaking.translation: Los expertos nos han advertido repetidamente que no [verbo]...

speaking.structure: The person in the first picture seems to be suggesting that...
speaking.example: The person in the first picture seems to be suggesting that teamwork is essential.
speaking.translation: La persona de la primera foto parece estar sugiriendo que...
